title: Bakery and Letters
premise: Casper Amberdale, a pastry chef whose café is three missed payments from gone, has trained her heart like any other muscle: contained, efficient, unneeded. When a letter postmarked eleven years ago surfaces inside her late grandmother's recipe tin — addressed to Casper's mother and mentioning a vineyard inheritance — it pulls her to the small town of Marrow Creek, where winemaker Theo Vance is the one person who never let her walk away. As the café deadline and the vineyard's first harvest collide, Casper must choose between the career that saved her from her family's silence and the man who sees her clearly at last. She chooses both: converting the café into a bakery-wine bar with Theo as partner, claiming the vineyard as shared inheritance with the found family she builds there.
about_author: Ivo Underhill is the pen name of a former line cook turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, cellars, and the quiet hours between shifts. They live above a bakery they refuse to name, on the theory that anonymity keeps the pastries honest.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The bank letter arrives during morning service at Amberdale Café; Casper folds it into her apron pocket and keeps piping choux like nothing happened. Her only employee, Dev, notices anyway. Emotional beat: controlled dread — Casper's habit of containing feeling before it can cost her anything.

chapters.title: The Recipe Tin
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Clearing out her grandmother's flat for rent money, Casper finds a sealed letter postmarked eleven years ago, addressed to her estranged mother, referencing 'the girl' and 'the vines at Marrow Creek.' She reads half of it and stops cold. Emotional beat: the first crack in Casper's containment — curiosity stronger than discipline.

chapters.title: Marrow Creek
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Leaving Dev to hold the café together, Casper drives to Marrow Creek and finds the vineyard half-abandoned, run by Theo Vance — a boy she knew one summer, eleven years ago, the summer everything went silent between her and her family. He recognizes her instantly; she pretends otherwise. Emotional beat: recognition as threat.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo reveals the rest: Casper's grandmother co-owned the vineyard, and the letter was her attempt to reconcile with Casper's mother before dying — an offer of inheritance that was never delivered. Theo has kept the land alive waiting for an answer. Emotional beat: grief arriving eleven years late.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Casper stays through harvest prep, trading pastry for labor; Theo teaches her the vines while she teaches him laminated dough. Dev calls daily with worsening café news. Emotional beat: warmth sneaking past training — Casper laughing for the first time in months.

chapters.title: The Muscle Remembers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A storm forces them into the cellar overnight; Theo tells Casper what really happened eleven years ago — that her mother asked him to lie to protect her, and he chose loyalty over truth. Casper walks out into the rain. Emotional beat: betrayal recontextualized; the heart refusing to stay containable.

chapters.title: Foreclosure
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The bank calls: final notice. Casper returns home to pack up the café and finds Dev has organized the neighborhood into a last-ditch pre-order campaign — and her mother, unannounced, sitting at the counter. Emotional beat: found family asserting itself whether Casper permits it or not.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Mother and daughter finally speak; Casper learns her grandmother's letter was hidden by her mother out of fear, not malice, and that the inheritance was meant for all of them. Forgiveness begins, unfinished. Emotional beat: memory reframed — the past wasn't abandonment, it was fear passed down.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Harvest day. Casper arrives at dawn having signed papers converting the café into a bakery-wine bar, with the vineyard held jointly by her, her mother, and Theo. But she nearly doesn't come — pride, old training — until Dev drives her himself. Emotional beat: climax; choosing people over armor.

chapters.title: Bakery and Letters
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Months later: the new shop opens, wine from the first harvest on shelves beside the bread, Dev running front of house, her mother managing the books. Casper writes her own letter — to her grandmother, read aloud at the vineyard table — thanking her for the inheritance no one could contain. Emotional beat: resolution; the heart, trainable after all, trained toward openness.
